label: End of long (L=9) inputs starting with n: last original token and <DEL>
explanation: Fires only at the end of the original phase of long sequences: the last original token (t=8 for L=9, ~t=7 for L=8) and the <DEL> step right after it. It never fires in the copy phase or before t=6. 86% of mass is on L=9 and 13% on L=8; L<=6 never fires. Firing depends strongly on the first original token: n carries 68% of mass (18x lift), then u, w, e, j at lower rates. Other first tokens rarely fire. Even within L=9 sequences that start with n, only about 29% fire. Digits or q/z/l/1 anywhere in the input, especially as the last token (1 and q are the strongest), raise firing rate and magnitude a little, but no simple token condition separates firing from non-firing sequences. The largest activations (about 3.0) are on a last original token of 1 in n-initial L=9 sequences. Using first_tok in {n,u,w,e,j} instead of n alone captures 92% of mass but precision drops to 5%.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=n (+7.91), orig0=u (+4.92), orig0=w (+4.07), orig0=e (+3.85), prev_tok=q (+3.57), orig2=m (+3.57). Lower it: next_out=- (-7.78), phase=2 (-7.66), orig7=- (-5.24), orig8=- (-3.11).
